name: Collab of the Year!

pick.label: Pick a brand
pick.heading: Pick a brand and find it a partner
lead: Some of the best products of the last few years came from two brands that have nothing in common. KFC and Crocs once made shoes that looked like a bucket of fried chicken. Really.
Choose a brand, find it the strangest partner you can, and make something together. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The stranger, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: I'm not looking for a real business plan here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some collabs will make total sense and some will only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: Who is the other half? Pick one that nobody would expect.
A product, a shop, an event, a limited edition?
Colours, logo, packaging. Whose style wins, or do you mix them?
Who buys it first, and why?
Where and when? Who's there? What will people post about it?

values.product: A flat-pack chocolate Easter bunny. You get 14 chocolate pieces, instructions with no words and a tiny Allen key, also made of chocolate.
values.look: IKEA blue and yellow on the box, Lindt's gold foil inside. The bunny is called HOPPLA, obviously.
values.who: Couples who want to test their relationship before they buy a wardrobe together.
values.launch: In the IKEA restaurant in Tempelhof at Easter. Build your bunny in under ten minutes and you get free meatballs. If you have pieces left over, you have to eat them.

yours.label: Your collab
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your collab in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which collab wins?
rank.placeholder: The collab, e.g. IKEA x Lindt
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their collab in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
